title: Battlefy: 83.6K accounts breached
summary: In January 2016, the esports website Battlefy suffered a data breach that exposed 83k customer records. The impacted data included email addresses, usernames and passwords stored as bcrypt hashes.

title: Shadi.com: 2M accounts breached
summary: In July 2016, the Muslim dating site Shadi.com suffered a data breach that exposed over 2M members' email addresses. The breach also exposed passwords stored as MD5 hashes alongside their plain text equivalents.

title: PPCGeeks: 492.5K accounts breached
summary: In August 2016, the pocket PC fan site forum PPCGeeks suffered a data breach that exposed over 490k records. The breach of the vBulletin forum exposed email and IP addresses, usernames, dates of birth and passwords stored as salted MD5 hashes.

title: JukinMedia: 314.3K accounts breached
summary: In October 2021, the "global leader in user-generated entertainment" Jukin Media suffered a data breach. The breach exposed 13GB of code, configuration and data consisting of 314k unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers, IP addresses and bcrypt password hashes.

title: Famm: 535.2K accounts breached
summary: In late 2020, the Japanese family photos website Famm suffered a data breach that subsequently exposed 1.3M customer records, including 535k unique email addresses. Impacted data also included names, dates of birth, genders and passwords stored as SHA-256 hashes.

title: Eskimi: 1.2M accounts breached
summary: In late 2020, the AdTech platform Eskimi suffered a data breach that exposed 26M records with 1.2M unique email addresses. The data included usernames, dates of birth, genders and passwords stored as unsalted MD5 hashes.

title: La Poste Mobile: 533.9K accounts breached
summary: In July 2022, the French telecommunications company La Poste Mobile was the target of an attack by the LockBit ransomware which resulted in company data being published publicly. title: Capital Economics: 263.8K accounts breached
summary: In December 2020, the economic research company Capital Economics suffered a data breach that exposed 263k customer records. The exposed data included email and physical addresses, names, phone numbers, job titles and the employer of impacted customers.
